name: WOFF2 to TTF/OTF font decompression
description:
HARNESS RULES FOR THIS GROUP: (a) the MAIN PATH below runs on every input with the full input, exactly as listed; it is the baseline, the rest of this Logic Group only adds to it. (b) Entries marked 'same core / alternative' reach the same internal code as the main call: never replace the main call with them and never run all of them on every input (fan-out kills exec/s); if used, run at most one of them as an extra step chosen by spare input bits. (c) A configuration switch must never take inputs away from the main path; options that only add code (e.g. detail/verbose output) stay ON. (d) This list is incomplete; what the project's own fuzzers, tests and examples do with the target stays in scope. (e) Nothing the fuzz input can make slow or hang may run on every input: no allocation sized from an untrusted header field, no call with a known library hang (listed below), no callback/selector that aborts the main call for a large share of inputs; the bytes handed to the parser start at a fixed offset (offset 0 when the format has a magic number), so the fuzzer can find magic numbers and header fields.
MAIN PATH (keep on every input; verified in woff2 (qf-work/src/woff2-c2) source):
1. size_t hint = woff2::ComputeWOFF2FinalSize(data, size). It only returns the untrusted 32-bit totalSfntSize field at offset 16 (src/woff2_dec.cc:1339-1348), so for random inputs it is usually tens of MB to 4 GB.
2. std::string buf; presize it from the hint ONLY when the hint is small (e.g. 0 < hint <= 1 MiB); otherwise leave it empty. WOFF2StringOut grows the string on demand (src/woff2_out.cc:20-35; include/woff2/output.h:53-55 "buf may be sized ... or empty"), so presizing is only a hint. Never allocate or zero-fill a buffer of min(hint, N MB) on every input.
3. woff2::WOFF2StringOut out(&buf); out.SetMaxSize(30 * 1024 * 1024) (include/woff2/output.h:62; woff2_out.cc:37-42).
4. bool ok = woff2::ConvertWOFF2ToTTF(data, size, &out) on the FULL input (woff2_dec.cc:1356; the WOFF2 header with the "wOF2" signature starts at offset 0, so no control bytes in front).
5. If ok: read back out.Size() bytes of buf (src/woff2_decompress.cc:35-38 uses output.begin() .. begin()+out.Size()).
The previous LG harness ran the deprecated fixed-buffer overload on every input with std::vector<uint8_t>(min(hint, 30 MB)); because the hint is a random u32, almost every input allocated and zeroed 30 MB, exec/s fell to 489 (w/o LG 2389) and in 30 min the fuzzer never got past ReadWOFF2Header into the brotli decoder (brotli dec 0 lines vs 1300+ for w/o LG).
ADDITIONS on top (spare input bits only): the deprecated overload ConvertWOFF2ToTTF(result, result_length, data, length) (same core / alternative: it wraps the same decoder with a WOFF2MemoryOut, woff2_dec.cc:1350-1354) only on a rare selector value and only with a small fixed buffer (<= 64 KiB, or out.Size() of a successful main call), never sized from the hint; a second SetMaxSize value (small max size) on spare bits to reach the Write() size-limit failure branch.

FEATURE DESCRIPTION (from the Logic Group stage):
ConvertWOFF2ToTTF takes a completely untrusted, attacker-controlled WOFF2 font file (raw bytes) and reconstructs it into a classic SFNT/TTF font: it parses the WOFF2 header and table directory, brotli-decompresses the compressed table data blob, and then walks every table applying format-specific "transforms" (most importantly reversing the custom glyf/loca delta-encoding and the hmtx compaction) while re-computing table checksums and offsets and streaming the rebuilt bytes to a WOFF2Out sink. Because the header lengths, per-table transform flags, substream sizes, glyph counts and metrics are all taken straight from the file, this is a classic "parse deeply nested untrusted binary format and rebuild a new binary" surface, rich in integer-overflow / bounds-check opportunities, which is exactly what the project's own fuzzer (convert_woff2ttf_fuzzer.cc) exercises.
- woff2::ConvertWOFF2ToTTF(data,length,out): target entry; top-level driver that reads the header, decompresses the payload with brotli, and reconstructs each font (handles plain WOFF2 and WOFF2 TTC collections).
- woff2::ConvertWOFF2ToTTF(result,result_length,data,length): deprecated overload/variant that wraps the WOFF2Out version with a WOFF2MemoryOut backed by a fixed caller-supplied buffer — a different output-sink path (fixed buffer vs growable string) worth exercising together with the main entry.
- woff2::ComputeWOFF2FinalSize(data,length): source/config helper that reads the (untrusted) totalSfntSize field from the header and is used by every real caller (CLI tool, fuzzer harness pattern) to size the output buffer/string passed to ConvertWOFF2ToTTF, so it feeds the state (buffer size) the target and its WOFF2Out implementation operate under.
Core internal functions reached from the target that implement the actual parsing/transform logic:
- ReadWOFF2Header: parses the fixed header, table directory (incl. Read255UShort variable-length encodings), and, when flavor == TTC, the collection header/ttc font list — this is the first attacker-controlled-length/branch point (plain font vs TTC, header_version 0x00010000/0x00020000, number of tables/fonts).
- WriteHeaders: builds the sfnt Offset Table and TableRecord directory (and TTC header when applicable) ahead of table bodies, validating table ordering/bounds.
- Woff2Uncompress: brotli-decompresses the compressed table block into the uncompressed_size computed from the header; the compression-ratio check (kMaxPlausibleCompressionRatio) and brotli's own decode state machine are exercised here.
- ReconstructFont: per-font driver that walks each table, decides whether it is stored raw or "transformed" (kWoff2FlagsTransform flag) and dispatches to the glyf/hmtx reconstructors, also validates the glyf/loca pairing invariant and recomputes checksums.
- ReconstructGlyf: reverses the WOFF2 transformed-glyf encoding — splits it into the 7 substreams (n_contour, n_points, flags, glyph, composite, bbox, instructions), rebuilds simple and composite glyph outlines point-by-point and regenerates the loca table; this is the most complex and bounds-sensitive state machine in the decoder.
- ReconstructTransformedHmtx: reverses the transformed hmtx table, branching on flag bits that select proportional vs monospace left-side-bearings reconstruction from stored x_mins.
Input space the harness should vary: file flavor (plain WOFF2 vs TTC via header.flavor==kTtcFontFlavor), header_version (0x00010000 / 0x00020000) and number of ttc fonts/tables, per-table transform flag bits (kWoff2FlagsTransform set or not, selecting raw-copy vs glyf/hmtx transform paths), presence/absence and matching of glyf+loca tables, the glyf transform version/flags word (FLAG_OVERLAP_SIMPLE_BITMAP), index_format (0=short/1=long loca), num_glyphs/num_hmetrics magnitudes, hmtx_flags bits (proportional/monospace lsbs), the declared vs actual compressed/uncompressed sizes (to hit the compression-ratio and brotli failure branches), and the choice of output sink (WOFF2StringOut with a settable SetMaxSize vs WOFF2MemoryOut with a fixed buffer from ComputeWOFF2FinalSize).
